subject: Cloud Computing
title: Zero Trust Security
description: A 60-second lesson on Zero Trust Security.

hook.text: Traditional security trusted everyone inside the network. Zero trust says: trust nobody, verify everything.

buildup.text: Zero trust verifies every request — even from inside the network. Location alone doesn't grant access.

discovery.text: Google pioneered zero trust with BeyondCorp after being hacked by Chinese state actors in 2009.

twist.text: Zero trust is a philosophy, not a product. Despite what vendors claim, you can't buy it in a box.

climax.text: Implementing zero trust takes years. But it's the only model that makes sense in a cloud-first world.

punchline.text: Trust nothing. Verify everything. That's zero trust.

quiz.question: What event prompted Google to develop the zero trust model?
options: A sophisticated hack by Chinese state-sponsored actors in 2009
A data center fire that destroyed customer data
A competing cloud provider stealing Google's source code

details.summary: Zero trust assumes no user, device, or network is trusted by default, even inside the corporate perimeter. Every access request is verified based on identity, device health, and context. It replaces the traditional castle-and-moat model that fails in cloud environments.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud dissolves the traditional network perimeter. Zero trust provides a security model that works when resources are distributed across providers, locations, and devices.
takeaways: Never trust, always verify every access request
Evaluates identity, device, location, and behavior
Replaces perimeter-based security for cloud environments

faq.question: How does zero trust differ from VPN-based security?
faq.answer: VPNs grant broad network access once connected, trusting anything inside the tunnel. Zero trust grants access only to specific resources after verifying identity, device posture, and context for each request. It provides much finer-grained control.

faq.question: Is zero trust a product or a strategy?
faq.answer: Zero trust is a strategy and architecture, not a single product. Implementing it involves combining identity verification, micro-segmentation, device health checks, and continuous monitoring. Many vendors sell components, but no single tool delivers full zero trust.
